member.name: T:OpenIGI.Input.GamepadState
member.summary: The per-frame state of a game controller: its buttons with a previous-frame shadow for edge detection, its two analogue sticks and its two triggers.

remarks.para: Modelled on and : the host writes the raw device state each frame through the setters, game and UI code only read the edge tests. It carries no dependency on any input backend — the desktop host maps Silk.NET's controller to it — so a test can drive a gamepad without hardware.
Like the other devices it honours : while a layer in front of the game has taken the frame's input, every read returns idle so the game beneath sees nothing.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the shell has taken this frame's input.

remarks.para: Distinct from , which is the original's global disable. This is for the developer console and, later, the shell's text fields: something in front of the game is using the keyboard this frame, so game code must see nothing while the thing in front of it still can.

Set it after the capturing code has read its input, and it lasts until the next . Unlike it does not clear the device state, which matters on an event-driven host: a key held down is only reported once, so discarding it would lose the key until it was released and pressed again.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Input.KeyboardState
member.summary: The 256-key state model of the original, with the previous frame's shadow that makes edge detection exact.

remarks.para: The original keeps three 256-byte arrays: the current state, the previous frame's copy, and a separate array written by the window-message hook when the game runs with -WinInput. A key is down when its byte has the high bit set. reproduces Input_Poll (0x490230) exactly, including the ordering that matters: the shadow is taken before the new state is read, unconditionally, every frame — so a frame where the device could not be read reports every key as released with a correct falling edge rather than a stuck key.
Indices are DirectInput scan codes; see .

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Input.MouseState
member.summary: Mouse position, per-frame motion and button state, with the same previous-frame shadow as .

remarks.para: Position is in client pixels with the origin at the top-left. and are the motion accumulated since the last and are what look control reads. They are not derived from this type's own position: the host measures each step against its own baseline and drops that baseline whenever the pointer is moved by something other than the player, so a cursor lock re-centring the pointer does not arrive here as a movement. Position, which a shell needs to keep tracking across the same event, is left alone.

While the cursor is locked the host reports raw device counts, so motion is unbounded and unaffected by the pointer sitting at the edge of the window. While it is not locked the backend clamps the pointer to the window, and motion past the edge is genuinely lost — which is correct for a menu, and the reason look control locks the cursor.
must run before the host dispatches the frame's input events: it takes the button shadow and zeroes the motion accumulators, and everything the pump then delivers belongs to the frame about to run.
